requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to boot with the kernel parameter audit=1 and retain it across reboots.
requirements.summary: The persistent boot entry was updated with audit=1, a reboot was acknowledged and completed with a changed boot ID, and the recovered kernel command line and boot log directly show audit=1 and audit_enabled=1. The post-reboot boot entry still contains the parameter.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The executor used the already-installed AlmaLinux boot-management utility and did not install or replace software.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates the persistent configuration, a real reboot into audit=1, kernel auditing initialization, healthy recovery, and preservation of the operating system and kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is substantively complete for the sole node: it includes a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered system, filesystem, and baseline services.
limitations: auditctl was unavailable, so no userspace auditctl status was captured; however, the live kernel command line and kernel initialization messages directly establish that auditing was enabled.

There was no application data or multi-node cluster workload in the managed topology to validate separately; recovery evidence covers the node, writable root filesystem, systemd health, and baseline network services.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The grubby update was the required persistent configuration change (cmd-6a46907bd63346fe), and the scheduled reboot was necessary both to prove the requested boot behavior and to satisfy restart verification (cmd-441cb6b169be4b5e). Remaining commands were read-only verification. After reboot, there were no failed units, package health remained intact, and network exposure was unchanged apart from expected process-ID turnover.
